conversation.content:
Good morning—I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician, and my job is simply to listen and understand how things have felt for you since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s ten questions about the past seven days; nothing you say is shared beyond the care team unless you or baby’s safety is at immediate risk. There are no right or wrong answers—just whatever is true for you today. Ready to begin?

1. Over the last seven days, have you still been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt hard to do?

*shifts in chair and gives a small shrug*

I can still laugh... sometimes. My sister came over yesterday and told a story about her work that made me chuckle. But mostly it feels like work to find things funny. My husband will make jokes like he always did, and I just... can't really get there. It's like there's this heaviness that makes everything feel kind of gray.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… maybe once or twice when my older niece was being silly, but even then it felt forced, like I had to remind myself “this is supposed to be funny.” Most of the time I just feel too tired or down to laugh.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

*eyes drop to my lap, voice softens*

I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park, even just a quiet shower. Now… nothing feels worth looking forward to. I still do them, but it’s like I’m just ticking boxes. The last seven days, when I think about tomorrow, I mostly feel dread that I’ll still be this exhausted and empty.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

*nods slowly, eyes welling up*

Yeah... like yesterday the baby wouldn't settle for his nap and I kept thinking it must be something I did—maybe I didn't swaddle him right, or I ate something that's upsetting him through the breast milk. When he finally fell asleep I just sat there crying, feeling like I'm failing him. My mom keeps saying babies are just fussy sometimes but I can't help feeling it's my fault when he cries.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

*nods quickly, twisting a tissue in my hands*

All the time. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s not getting enough milk, even though the pediatrician says she’s gaining fine. At night I lie there imagining the crib blanket somehow covering her face, so I jump up to check every hour. I know it sounds crazy, but the worries just pop in and won’t leave.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

*wrings the tissue tighter, voice shaking*

Yes… a few nights this week I woke up suddenly and my heart was pounding, I couldn’t catch my breath. It felt like something awful was about to happen, even though the room was quiet and the baby was sleeping. I checked the locks, the stove, the baby’s breathing—everything was fine, but the fear just sat on my chest. It lasted maybe twenty minutes before I could lie back down.
Things have been getting on top of me

*blinks back tears, voice cracking*

Most days, yeah. Like this morning—she wouldn’t latch, the laundry’s piled up, and I couldn’t even find a clean burp cloth. I just sat on the couch crying with her still in my arms, feeling like I’m drowning in stuff that used to be simple. I eventually get through it, but it feels like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

*exhales shakily*

Yes… even when the baby finally sleeps, my mind keeps spinning. I lie there thinking I’m doing everything wrong, replaying every cry, every fussy moment. Some nights I drift off for maybe twenty minutes, then jerk awake with this rush of sadness and can’t settle again. I probably only get three or four broken hours total, and I wake up already feeling defeated.
I have felt sad or miserable

*voice drops, eyes fixed on the floor*

Pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this heavy cloud that won’t lift. I see other moms posting happy pictures and I wonder why I can’t feel that joy. I love my baby, but this sadness just sits in my chest, and some evenings I end up crying while I rock her, feeling so guilty that I’m not happier.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

*nods, dabbing at eyes with the crumpled tissue*

Yes… it’s happened three, maybe four times this week. Yesterday I put her in the car seat to go to the grocery store and the strap got twisted—something tiny—and I just broke down. I sat on the floor sobbing, feeling like I can’t even do the simplest things right.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

*shakes head quickly*

No… never. I get overwhelmed and sad, but I would never want to leave my baby or hurt myself. I just want to feel better so I can be the mom she deserves.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Postpartum mother, 7–14 days post-delivery, no self-harm ideation reported.

Key symptoms endorsed  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, hopelessness (Q8, Q9)  
- Marked anhedonia and loss of anticipatory pleasure (Q1, Q2)  
- Excessive self-blame and guilt regarding infant care (Q3)  
- Generalized anxiety, nocturnal panic attacks, intrusive catastrophic worries about infant safety (Q4, Q5)  
- Subjective overwhelm, “drowning” in routine tasks (Q6)  
- Mood-congruent insomnia (even when infant sleeps) (Q7)

Patterns / risk indicators  
- Symptoms present daily over past week, causing functional impairment in self-care and infant care.  
- No evidence of psychosis or self-harm intent (Q10); protective factor: strong motivation to care for infant.  
- Obstetric history, support system, and prior psychiatric history not assessed in this screen.

Screening impression  
High clinical concern for postpartum major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; meets threshold for immediate follow-up with OB/midwife and referral to mental health specialty for comprehensive evaluation and possible treatment.
